experiments.verdict: Adopt. One loader reads the work packet once and forks one pass per drill unit, the structural pass and the cold editor: every fork starts from about 100k cached tokens and finishes in 2 or 3 responses. Review cost falls 80% and the run 62%, review time from 28 to 106 minutes to 5, with recall, applied edits and rewrite safety all within the baseline noise band. Constraints: forks share the loader model, cannot fork again, and the current workflow tool cannot host them, so the review runs as a loader agent the session spawns.

experiments.evidence: Across the graded runs of 13 Oct (02b, 02c), 14 Oct and 2 Oct, only 5% to 17% of verification candidates sat in clusters ignored on a rule that does not depend on the verdict (H-03, H-05, H-08, H-09, H-11, H-12, H-15, H-19, H-23, H-25, H-28). The hypothesis needed at least 30%. Most ignores are H-29, which the verdict itself causes, so grading first cannot skip them.

results.move_agreement_exact: 0.83 and 0.75 against the two Opus triages (noise floor 0.83)

experiments.verdict: Reject. One closer per page saves 15% of triage (about $0.23 a page) but its claim verdicts fall below the Opus noise floor (85-89% against 96%): verifying and grading in one context weakens the independent check. Triage is a small share of a run; the review side is where structure pays.

experiments.verdict: Mixed. Rewrites become far safer (H-29 ignores -79%, material verdicts -75%) and the run is 11% cheaper, but reviewers drop risky rewrites into questions, so 31% fewer edits apply and the fixes differ from the baseline (recall 0.44 against a 0.80 noise floor). Whether the different fixes are better is a quality judgement: into the blind pack for Ben.

experiments.idea: I12 brief stops asking for kinds the rubric ignores
experiments.evidence: Pooled 374 graded clusters from five runs: 178 ignored, 120 of them by H-29 (the rewrite failed verification) and 58 on rules independent of the verdict. No kind exceeds 35% verdict-independent ignores; the high overall ignore rates of omission (82%), fact (83%) and expand (83%) come from failed rewrites. Only the action ask is ignored on its face (14 of 25, 56%, mostly H-08 design questions). The remaining test: stop asking reviewers for design questions; the larger effect belongs to X7.

experiments.idea: I1 delta review for changed heuristics
experiments.reframe: The latest heuristic change (06fcec6, FAQ voice) has no instances in the corpus, which already passes the gate. X11 tests the idea instead: a review limited to one changed rule body (the Terms rules: language.md lines 114-126 and ubiquitous-language.md) against the full review B0c on C3.

runs.config: 3 delta reviewers (Opus), one per page, reading a 17 KB delta packet, their page and the set digest; findings into review/*.json; triage as baseline
runs.ground_truth: B0c clusters of kind term and their fixes

results.term_findings: 28 against the full review's 10 term clusters
results.verdict_material: 3 of 24 rewrites (12.5%) against about a third in full reviews
results.metric_note: cost.review shows 0 because the stage classifier does not know the delta role; the delta reviewers are in cost.total

experiments.verdict: Adopt as a mode, not a replacement. To apply a changed rule to pages already reviewed, a delta review limited to that rule costs a third of a full run, finds nearly three times as many findings under the rule and applies 10 fixes against the full review's 3, with safer rewrites. It finds only 4 of the full review's 10 term clusters and none of the other kinds, so a full review remains the tool for a page that has not been reviewed.

experiments.verdict: Fallback. tests.name: layer 0 reach (offline)
tests.ground_truth: 299 distinct findings (149 fixed by some run) from every experiment workarea on the frozen pages

results.detector_precision: 0.67 to 1.00 (long sentence 0.86, near-duplicate 0.83, passive 0.71, forbidden term 1.00)

by_owning_layer.paragraph: 172 findings (58%), 98 fixed (57%): ambiguity, compression, term, flow, absolute, residue

tests.verdict: Layer 0 catches little on pages that already pass the gate (11-13%); its value is precise attention pointers for the paragraph layer and authoring-time checks. Repetition is semantic (1 of 39 caught textually), so it belongs to the set layer. Term findings are concept naming, which a register of preferred names could mechanise. The strongest result: design-consistency findings are 26% of all findings and only 14% become fixes, which supports a separate facts track that outputs questions, not rewrites.

tests.name: design-consistency facts track
tests.config: one Opus extractor per page (00, 02a, 02b, 02c) writes structured facts (actor, action, object, condition, force, value, quote); facts merged into one register sorted by actor and object (898 facts, rejected-design facts dropped); one Opus checker reads only the register and lists contradictions
tests.ground_truth: 26 distinct contradiction or reconcile findings from every experiment run on 02a, 02b and 02c; 16 raised by three or more runs; the cookie contradiction at 02a lines 14 and 29

results.reported_new: 3, all S2, on delegation and provider credentials, plausibly real

cost.note: extraction includes the 00 and 02c agents presumed lost to a network outage and re-run; the original 02c agent finished at 16:37, after the register was built, and its later turns are not counted; its 231-fact file is kept as runs/R2/late-02c-ins-auth-session-api-16-37.json and was not used

tests.caveat: the match is loose (a reported contradiction within one line of a finding or its related lines), so one reported contradiction can cover several findings; the 3 new contradictions need Ben to judge
tests.verdict: The facts track is the redesign's strongest lever: it finds nearly every contradiction the reviews found across all runs, where one review run finds a quarter to a half, at about half the cost of a full review, and its register is reusable: re-extract only changed pages, re-run the $1.18 check.

tests.name: facts track repeat, with section, table and column fields
tests.config: R2 repeated with the same extractor and checker prompts; the extractor also records each fact's section, and for a table row what the table lists and the column header; the register lines carry them (972 facts, 254 KB against 898 and 188 KB)

results.robust_found: 15 of 16; missed 02b:88, the lastSeenAt reader, a prose line R2 caught
results.overlap_with_R2: all 18 R2 contradictions have an R2r counterpart by cited facts within one line; R2r adds 2 S3
results.recurring_new: the front door querying the delegation grant source with its own keys (S1 in R2r, S2 in R2); sub fixed as the contact identifier while elsewhere conditional on IDM not using a pairwise value

caveats: the checker cited the 12 Oct CDP meeting from workspace memory, outside the register, in its note on K-001; K-002 (sign-out GET against form POST) rests on 02a:157, which is in the register, so only the note drew on memory
the 00 extractor recorded working assumptions with force may, which R2's did not
tests.verdict: The facts track is stable: one run finds 88 to 96% of the contradictions every review run raised together, and two runs agree almost entirely. The table and column fields made no measurable difference and made the check 33% dearer; drop them unless a later miss traces to a table. The checker's prompt should forbid outside knowledge.

tests.name: layered review (paragraph, page and set passes) on C3
tests.config: one Opus loader reads a packet holding the brief's shared sections, three layer cards (questions verbatim from the brief, split by the redesign spec's map) and 55 layer 0 pointers, then forks a paragraph pass and a page pass per page and one set pass; no pass reports contradictions; findings through the X9 triage workflow; facts from R2 and R2r

recall_by_kind.contradiction: 1 of 3, handed to the facts track

tests.diagnosis: Repetition is 39% of the baselines' fixes, and the set pass returned one repetition finding: the R3 set card gave one pass for the whole set a cap of 6 redundancies and 12 findings, where P1's three page-scoped structural reviewers had up to 18 redundancies between them. The setup throttled the commonest fix kind; this is not evidence against layering.
tests.verdict: Not passed as set up: recall 0.47 against the 0.49 line. The layering's quality gains are beyond noise: rewrites the verifier finds meaning-changing fall 59%, H-29 ignores 55%, the ignore rate from 0.55 to 0.40, and it finds the most new fixes of any run, at the package's cost. Next test: one set pass per page (repetition and cross-page references anchored on that page, the set as context) at P1's caps.

tests.name: layered review with one set pass per page on C3
tests.config: R3 unchanged except the set card: one set pass per reviewed page, the whole set as context, findings anchored on that page, worked paragraph by paragraph, capped at 12 findings, 6 redundancies and 2 patterns per page; nine forks from one Opus loader; same X9 triage
tests.verdict: Passed. Recall 0.62 equals the agreement between two baseline runs, the best of any cheaper arm, with 20 new fixes and 39 applied edits at the package's cost (-47% against the baselines), and the rewrite-safety gains of R3 hold. Per-page set passes recovered repetition (16 of 25 against R3's 9), confirming R3's diagnosis. One run: P1 and its repeat differed by 0.09 in recall, and the extra fixes need Ben's blind judgement (R3b is in the C3 blind pack).

tests.name: incremental re-review, scoped and with settled findings

tests.verdict: The scope holds: 19 findings against 50, no settled finding raised again, so the triage and the author handle only what the edits touched. The review itself costs about the same as a full one, because every fork carries the whole packet; a smaller re-review packet is the next lever if that matters.
